title: ttr-lexicon/v1 — alias / value / grounding-trigger / string-predicate data file
description: A lexicon data file in the defining repo's sibling data area (`lexicon/aliases/*.lex.yaml`, `lexicon/values/*.lex.yaml`, `lexicon/grounding/*.lex.yaml`, `lexicon/predicates/*.lex.yaml`). RV-36..38, RV-42, LP §3; contracts §2. Entry KIND is not declared here — it is derived from the target class (RV-38).

schema.description: Ledger id. Must equal the id of the schema the file is validated against.

defaults.description: Per-file defaults. A term's own `lang`/`method`/`match` always wins.

lang.description: BCP-47-lite: a single language or the both-languages form `cs|en`.

method.description: Match method. TYPOS carries its edit budget inline: TYPOS(1)..TYPOS(3).

match.description: RV-44 — a declared matching profile: which normalized forms count for this term and how strong each is. Order is convention (strongest first); combination across firings is MAX, so a mis-ordered list gives identical results. `method:` is sugar for one of three profiles (EXACT / TYPOS(d) / TOKENS) and the two are mutually exclusive on one node. Contracts §2 addendum; design/06-M.

norm.description: The normalization stratum this rule compares on. CLOSED set (M-T2): `canonical` = NFC + lowercase, diacritics preserved; `folded` = canonical + diacritics stripped; `lemma` = per-token lemmatization. There is deliberately no case-sensitive stratum.

exact.description: Equality on this norm scores here. The declared score is the WITHIN-class score (`in_class_score`) — RV-14's evidence classes still decide, scores only order inside one.

typos.description: Bounded edit distance on this norm. Fires at `exact − d·penalty` for 1 ≤ d ≤ distance, so it needs a sibling `exact` on the same norm as its anchor. Suppressed by the short-term guard when the authored term's canonical form is ≤ 3 characters (⚑M-4 — a build warning, not an error).

tokens.description: Token-set matching on this norm (the engine's own algorithm, with the RV-32 uniqueness margin). No keys yet — the object is the extension point.

target.description: Any model-graph ref (`er.*`, `md.*`, member refs), an `op:` ref, a `ground:` class ref (RV-42), or a `pred:` string-predicate ref (LP contracts §3). Existence of a MODEL ref is checked at compile time against the model snapshot, not here — but the `ground:` and `pred:` vocabularies ARE closed, because each names a consumer that must implement the behaviour: a kernel that loads the slice, a consumer that lowers the predicate (kantheon's fast-path renderer, e.g. `pred:starts_with` ⇒ `col LIKE ? || '%' ESCAPE …`). The `pred:` FORM rules are Kotlin-only: RG-LEX-031 (no single-character or function-word trigger, and no phrase of function words only) needs a per-language word list, which JSON Schema cannot carry; RG-LEX-032 (at most `LexiconValidator.MAX_PREDICATE_FORM_TOKENS` = 3 words) counts tokens on the Kotlin normalizer's whitespace, and a second definition of a token here would be one more thing to drift.
